title: Separable approximate roots of a uniformizer
statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic $p$, with fraction field $E$ and uniformizer $\pi$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-pc-field-extension]. For every integer $r\geq1$, $q=p^r$, and integer $h>1$, there is a separable field extension $E_1/E$ of degree $q$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] whose integral closure $R_1$ of $R$ is a complete discrete valuation ring [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], with $R_1/\mathfrak m_{R_1}=R/\mathfrak m_R$ and $\mathfrak m_RR_1=\mathfrak m_{R_1}^{q}$. It has a uniformizer $t$ and elements $b,b'\in R_1$ satisfying $t^q=\pi+\pi^h b=\pi+t^{hq}b'$.

source.place: Tag 09EW, lemma-make-degree-q-extension, equicharacteristic-p specialization; completeness of the finite normalization over the complete base.

proof.text: Put $N=h+q-1$ and $f(X)=X^q-\pi^NX-\pi\in R[X]$. Since $r\geq1$ and $p$ is prime, $q\geq2$; hence $f$ is monic of degree $q$. Its nonleading coefficients belong to $\pi R$, and its constant coefficient $-\pi$ does not belong to $\pi^2R$: otherwise cancelling the nonzero $\pi$ in the domain $R$ would make $\pi$ a unit. Apply lem-sfb-eisenstein-quotient-dvr to obtain the DVR $C=R[X]/(f)$ with uniformizer $t=[X]$. By lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free, $1,t,\ldots,t^{q-1}$ is an $R$-basis of $C$; in particular $R\to C$ is injective and $C$ is finite free of rank $q$.

source.place: Tag 09EW, lemma-make-degree-q-extension, characteristic-p proof, after y=pi z

proof.text: Localize the displayed basis at $R\setminus\{0\}$, obtaining a domain $D=E[X]/(f)=E[t]$ with $E$-basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{q-1}$. For any nonzero $a\in D$, multiplication by $a$ is an injective endomorphism of the finite-dimensional $E$-vector space $D$, hence surjective; a preimage of $1$ is its inverse. Thus $D$ is a field. It contains $C$ and every fraction of elements of $C$, so $E_1:=D=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$, $E_1=E(t)$, and $[E_1:E]=q$. The basis also shows that no nonzero polynomial of degree less than $q$ vanishes at $t$, so the monic relation $f$ is its minimal polynomial.

source.place: Tag 09EW, lemma-make-degree-q-extension, characteristic-p proof, after y=pi z

proof.text: In characteristic $p$, the derivative of $X^q$ is zero since $p\mid q$. Consequently $f\prime=-\pi^N\ne0$ is a constant in $E[X]$. The explicit Bezout identity $0\cdot f+(-\pi^{-N})f\prime=1$ shows that $f$ is separable by def-pc-separable-polynomial. Since it is the minimal polynomial of $t$, the element $t$ is separable algebraic over $E$. Apply lem-trf-simple-separable-field-extension and $E_1=E(t)$ to obtain that the whole degree-$q$ extension $E_1/E$ is separable.

source.place: Tag 09EW, lemma-make-degree-q-extension, characteristic-p proof, after y=pi z

proof.text: The element $t$ is integral over $R$, being a root of the monic $f$. The integral closure of $R$ in $E_1$ is a subring containing $R$ and $t$, so it contains $C=R[t]$. Conversely, $C$ is a DVR, hence a valuation ring by the characterization in def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, and is integrally closed in its fraction field $E_1$ by lem-weil-pbc-valuation-ring-normal. If $z\in E_1$ is integral over $R$, its same monic equation has coefficients in $C$, so $z$ is integral over $C$ and belongs to $C$. Therefore the integral closure $R_1$ is exactly $C$.

source.place: Tag 09EW, lemma-make-degree-q-extension, characteristic-p proof, after y=pi z

proof.text: The relation $f(t)=0$ reads $t^q=\pi(1+\pi^{N-1}t)$. Put $u=1+\pi^{N-1}t$. Since $\mathfrak m_C=(t)$, the image of $u$ in the residue field is $1$, so $u$ is a unit. Thus $(\pi)C=(t^q)=\mathfrak m_C^q$. Killing $t$ in the presentation gives $C/(t)=R[X]/(X,f)=R/(\pi)$, via the canonical residue map. This proves precisely the claimed equality of residue fields (identified by this canonical isomorphism) and the claimed extended-maximal-ideal formula.

source.place: Tag 09EW, lemma-make-degree-q-extension, characteristic-p proof, after y=pi z

proof.text: All ideals of the DVR $R$ are principal, so $R$ is Noetherian. The finite free $R$-module $C$ is therefore $(\pi)$-adically complete by lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian, since the base $R$ is complete. Step 5 gives $\pi^kC=(t^{qk})$. These powers are cofinal among all $(t^m)$: a compatible family modulo $t^m$ restricts to one modulo $t^{qk}$, and conversely its coordinate modulo $t^m$ is the image of any coordinate modulo $t^{qk}$ with $qk\geq m$, independent of $k$ by compatibility. These two operations are inverse and preserve the canonical map from $C$. Thus $C=R_1$ is complete also for its own maximal ideal $(t)$.

source.place: Tag 00MA, lemma-completion-tensor (3); Tag 0317, definition-complete; cofinal powers spelled out for (pi)C=(t^q)

proof.text: Finally set $b=\pi^{q-1}t\in R_1$. The defining equation gives $t^q=\pi+\pi^{h+q-1}t=\pi+\pi^h b$. Since $t^q=\pi u$ and $u$ is a unit, $\pi^h=t^{hq}u^{-h}$. Taking $b\prime=u^{-h}b\in R_1$ yields $t^q=\pi+t^{hq}b\prime$. These are the two required approximation identities for the same uniformizer $t$.

source.place: Tag 09EW, lemma-make-degree-q-extension, characteristic-p proof, after y=pi z
